topic: Geometric Interpretation of Non-Square Matrices as Dimensional Transformations

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Linear Map
lecture_lines: Matrices are functions mapping vectors between spaces.
Square matrices stay in the same dimension.
Non-square matrices change the space dimension.
animations: Fade in a 2D vector 'v' (#FFFFFF) and a 3D vector 'Av' (#ADD8E6).
Animate transformation arrow from 'v' to 'Av' in #FFFF00.
Display text 'L(u+v) = L(u)+L(v)' in #90EE90 to show linearity.

sections.title: Dimensional Expansion (m > n): The Embedding
lecture_lines: Rows greater than columns mean expansion.
We embed a lower-dimensional object inside.
animations: Show 2D plane embedded inside 3D space 'R^3' in #FFD700.
Display label 'Embedding: R^2 to R^3' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Dimensional Compression (m < n): The Projection
lecture_lines: Columns greater than rows mean compression.
High-dimensional data squashes into smaller spaces.
Depth and detail are lost during projection.
animations: Show volume projected onto 2D plane 'R^2' in #FF4500.
Display label 'Projection: R^3 to R^2' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Null Space: What gets lost?
lecture_lines: Multiple inputs can map to one output.
Mapping becomes non-reversible in this case.
animations: Show vector 'x' inside the null space in #FF0000.
Highlight the origin point in #FFFFFF as the destination.
Animate 'x' shrinking into the origin labeled 'Loss'.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Matrices manipulate space through linear transformation.
Expansion creates room for higher-dimensional modeling.
Compression simplifies complex datasets for analysis.
animations: Fade in 'Linear Maps: Expansion & Compression' in #FFFFFF.
Animate split screen: Embedding on left, Projection on right.
